name: Nemotron-Labs-Sigma 3B and 8B (continuous diffusion language models)

lineage.base_model: autoregressive Ministral-style decoder, warm-started (about 1T tokens AR initialization, then about 0.3T tokens continuous-diffusion training)
lineage.family: Nemotron-Labs (diffusion line, same corpus as Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion)
lineage.how_derived: continuous-diffusion training in a 16-D token-embedding space; base, instruct and few-step distilled variants for 3B and 8B

purpose: Research models for diffusion-based parallel text generation: sampling, few-step distillation, trajectory steering and fine-tuning into assistants. The base card says it is not an instruction-following assistant (use the instruct repos).

license.name: NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License
license.notes: The cards say 'ready for commercial or non-commercial use' under this license; the license page (nvidia.com) returned only script code to the fetch tool and no LICENSE file is in the repo, so the text was not read (2026-11-19). Terms on redistribution and derivative models unknown.

architecture.kind: continuous diffusion language model on a Ministral-style transformer (GQA, SwiGLU, RoPE)
architecture.drafter: none; the paper reports one-step speculative decoding on the distilled 8B model
architecture.why_this_design: Paper abstract: denoising smooth continuous embeddings allows few-step distillation (about 8x on math, 4x on code) and embedding-space steering that improves pass@k; masked (discrete) diffusion baselines are outperformed, largest gains on coding. Card: block-parallel decoding (default 64 tokens per block, DDIM or DDPM samplers, classifier-free guidance, self-conditioning, KV cache for committed blocks).

variants.notes: the card also mentions -distill-* variants for fixed few-step decoding; their repos were not opened

pc-12gb.notes: 3B 7.7 GB fits; 8B 17 GB does not without quantization (none exists)

pc-16gb.notes: 8B BF16 17 GB exceeds the 13.6 GB budget

mac-16-24gb.notes: card requires CUDA; no MPS or CPU path (CPU output is unusable per the card)

mac-32gb.notes: 17 GB against about 22 GB GPU share, but the card supports only CUDA

other: PyTorch >= 2.4 + Transformers >= 4.55 with trust_remote_code, CUDA only
engine_support.notes: Custom sampler in plain PyTorch; the card states CPU inference degrades the sampler numerically. No GGUF found.

benchmarks.name: Few-step distillation speed-up
benchmarks.variant: distilled models, size not attributed in the abstract

strengths: Parallel block decoding with few-step distillation as a research direction
Reported coding gains over masked-diffusion baselines (vendor abstract)
weaknesses: Raw benchmark scores are only in the PDF, not on the card
soft.behavior: DDIM sampler recommended; quality drops noticeably below about 16 steps for the pretrained models, the distilled variants need no guidance tuning.
soft.maturity: Research release by NVIDIA labs, very few downloads (a few hundred per repo), no community reports found.

tona_fit.reason: 4K context, English only, CUDA-only custom sampler, no quantization or GGUF, research purpose; useful only as a technique reference for diffusion decoding (see also diffusiongemma-26b-a4b-it in the database).

sources.note: README and config read; 3B card assumed analogous (same repo layout, not read)
abstract read through a page summarizer (WebFetch); full PDF not read
license URL named by the card; page content not readable
